briefing: No new blockbuster financial data emerged since the last cycle, so this run layers in adjacent signal: Seeking Alpha's earnings check-in shows the ROI split hardening at the company level -- Microsoft posting strong free cash flow despite rising capex while Alphabet and Meta report negative or near-zero FCF, feeding investor skepticism even as chip and equipment suppliers keep benefiting. On the product/adoption side, Meta's Muse agent reportedly overtook ChatGPT as the No.1 US iPhone app and Anthropic says Claude now leads 26% of its own R&D work (a proof point for internal AI-driven productivity, if not yet external enterprise ROI), while Alibaba shipped Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash, keeping pressure on frontier pricing per Ramp's commoditization trend. Policy momentum continues to build in parallel to the ROI debate: California's governor advanced an executive order for AI 'kill switch' authority and onsite frontier-lab audits, and Anthropic/OpenAI/Microsoft face a newly unsealed NYT copyright-suit document. None of this changes the core thesis from the last run -- OpenAI's own $278B cash-burn forecast and Ramp's enterprise spend deceleration remain the dominant AI-trade risk signals -- but it reinforces that the market is now discriminating sharply between hyperscalers on FCF discipline rather than treating 'AI capex' as a single bloc.

items.headline: Leaked OpenAI deck: $278B negative free cash flow through 2030, cash could run out by 2028
items.summary: A confidential July presentation reviewed by the Financial Times shows OpenAI projecting cumulative negative free cash flow of $278B from 2026-2030 against ~$856B in compute/infrastructure spend, with revenue rising from $36B this year to $350B in 2030; the March $122B raise could be exhausted by 2028, prompting new fundraising talks near a $1.2T valuation.

items.headline: Ramp AI Index: top enterprise AI spend per employee fell ~10% in August as token prices collapse 41%
items.summary: Ramp's September AI Index found median AI spend per employee among the top 1% of spenders fell from $7,976 to $7,205 in August, while the effective price per million tokens dropped 41% since March to $0.68 and frontier-model token share slipped from 53% to 45% as enterprises rotated to cheaper standard models.

items.headline: Anthropic reportedly planning November IPO at ~$2T valuation
items.summary: Anthropic is said to be planning to IPO in November despite ongoing AI-safety concerns, targeting a roughly $2 trillion valuation and up to $100 billion raised, with annualized revenue reportedly above $110 billion.

items.headline: Earnings check-in: Microsoft's FCF holds up while Alphabet and Meta report negative or near-zero FCF
items.summary: A Seeking Alpha review of recent hyperscaler earnings finds a widening gap between capex and returns, with Microsoft emerging as a benchmark for strong free cash flow despite rising capex while Alphabet and Meta posted negative or near-zero free cash flow, deepening investor skepticism even as chipmakers and equipment suppliers keep benefiting from broadening spend.

items.headline: Meta's Muse AI agent reportedly overtakes ChatGPT as No. 1 US iPhone app
items.summary: AI Weekly reports Meta's Muse agent has climbed to the top of the US iPhone App Store charts, displacing ChatGPT, a notable shift in the consumer AI-assistant market that OpenAI has dominated since ChatGPT's launch.

items.headline: California advances executive order for AI 'kill switch' authority and onsite frontier-lab audits
items.summary: California's governor moved forward an executive order granting state authority to trigger an AI 'kill switch' and conduct onsite audits of frontier AI labs, part of a broader wave of state-level AI oversight action.

items.headline: Anthropic says Claude now leads 26% of its own R&D work
items.summary: Anthropic disclosed that Claude leads roughly 26 percent of the company's research and development, which the Washington Post frames as an indicator of progress toward AI that can improve itself with less human involvement.

items.headline: Nvidia reportedly weighing up to $10B check into Anthropic's IPO
items.summary: Reuters reports Nvidia is considering an investment as large as $10 billion tied to Anthropic's planned IPO, deepening the circular-investment pattern investors are watching in the AI trade.

items.headline: Sam Altman rules out 2026 OpenAI IPO, citing AI-safety concerns
items.summary: Altman told Fortune OpenAI will not go public in 2026 despite having confidentially filed for an IPO in June, saying the listing remains in the works but not on an immediate timetable as the company weighs a new private round instead.

items.headline: Alibaba ships Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash, an omni-modal agentic model with 1M-token context
items.summary: Alibaba released Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash, a native audio-video model built for agentic tool use with a 1M-token context window, performing close to Gemini 3.8 Flash on multimodal benchmarks, part of the continued frontier price/performance pressure Ramp's data shows enterprises exploiting.
